title: Why Reindeer Eyes Turn Blue in Winter
description:
Why do reindeer eyes turn blue in winter? In summer they shine gold; in midwinter the same eyes glow deep blue. Behind each eye is a mirror layer that bounces light back through it for a second chance to see. In the Arctic winter the sun stays down for weeks, so their pupils stay wide open. Scientists think fluid then can't drain properly, pressure builds, and it squeezes the mirror's tiny fibres closer together. Packed tighter, the mirror reflects blue, the colour of Arctic twilight, and less light escapes the eye, so reindeer see more in the dark.
